graphEvents.label: What should the hook-health default be and what does it cost
A diagnostic record costs about 200 bytes and 0.26 ms
Doctor hook health needs a record that only debug writes

label: The debug gate is one early return in writeBoundedJsonl, so the only choices today are one full record per prompt or nothing; outcome records already bypass it.
The reader needs durationMs, cacheHit and status only; it never reads skillLabel, emittedBytes, directivesSuppressed or errorDetails.

A default install can never show hook health: the doctor leg needs a record and the install prove-it step never sets SKILL_ADVISOR_DEBUG; 17 diagnostics files exist against 119 outcome files on this machine.
A record costs 196 bytes measured over 240 writes, and the live hook's records average 201.7 bytes; a health-only record would be about 120 bytes.

The append costs 0.26 ms median and 1.96 ms p95, and 30 alternating hook pairs give a paired delta median of -4.69 ms, so the write is below the hook's noise floor; the flush wait is capped at 100 ms.
Growth is bounded at 200 records with a trim past 300 lines, so 40 KB steady state and 60 KB worst transient per workspace in the OS temp directory.
The privacy cost of default-on is the skill id per prompt, not the prompt: the schema forbids prompt fields and the files are 0600, but skillLabel records which skill the person used.
Only the Claude hook adapter writes diagnostic records, so a default flip covers four of the six behaviour runtimes and leaves OpenCode and DSH with no health.
The opt-in gate was justified by nobody reading the records; since phase 011 advisor_status and /doctor:setup do read them, which is the new fact that reopens the default.
